name: PT Astra International Tbk

frontmatter.title: Astra International: fuel-efficient demand, a split October and a re-bracketed sum of the parts
frontmatter.summary: The industry body now gives the reason for the October split: buyers are trading up to fuel-efficient cars, so Toyota added 7.7% while Daihatsu moved -6.8% in a market of 81,482 units. National wholesales were 760,476 over ten months. This revision re-brackets the automotive mark, carries the toll book at the parent's economic interest, prices the rupiah path and mirrors the two scenario tails. HOLD at Rp4,692.
thesis: The group share is slipping on the measured pair: 49.0% over nine months against the level its own growth rates imply for the prior year — Astra up 13.0% in a market up 21.0% — about three and a half points; the 51.0% in the FY2025 release is worded "can reach", not an actual, so it is not used in that arithmetic, and October's visible table is about forty-six per cent [S4, S14, S31, S33, F14, F57, F125, F187, F179, F102].

The month itself is a mix shift, and the industry body supplies the cause: buyers are rotating to fuel-efficient vehicles at high fuel prices, so Toyota gained 7.7% and Daihatsu moved -6.8%, leaving the two brands flat at a little over two fifths of the October market; BYD's 6,639 wholesale is dealer stocking, with retail down to 6,355, only a hair above Suzuki's 6,284 [S34, S31, S33, S20, F180, F182].

The parts are worth Rp4,389 after the 35% discount, the automotive block at the midpoint of its two sourced multiples rather than at the top; un-rolled, the parts plus the Rp399 dividend sit below the Rp5,000 price, and the roll takes the expected return to 1.8% [S0, S15, S25, S32].

The floors are disclosed and now mirrored: about twenty-one trillion rupiah of Others-segment book equity sits outside the marks, held at zero in the base and realised at book in the bull, while the bear carries its quantified operating breaks; the toll concession rights are marked at the parent's 80.1% interest in Marga Mandalasakti, not at the whole of the consolidated book value [S15, F192, F193, F196].

The financing block is on its annualised actual return, the unlisted blocks at sourced floors, and parent G&A is already inside the segment incomes; the tails are discount-path probabilities, with the operating legs quantified in the text [S14, S15, S5, F78]

catalysts.event: Astra voluntary tender offer for Astra Otoparts closes
FY2026 audited results, final dividend and buyback-execution disclosure

frontmatter.catalyst_note: No dated discount-narrowing catalyst exists. The buyback approved at the 17 July 2026 EGM is authorised and ongoing with no disclosed end date or pace [S8, S14, S16]; the dated capital-allocation event is the Otoparts tender close, which lifts an already consolidated stake rather than upstreaming value to the holdco [S13, S14].

blocks.text: **What changed, and why the target moved.** This is a revision, not a news update: two marks move, the discount rule is stated, and the two scenario tails are mirrored in content as well as in their discount shocks. First, the automotive bracket bottom is Astra Otoparts' own TRAILING multiple — FY2025 profit of IDR2.35tn [S6] over the tender-implied share count at the Rp3,260 close, about six point seven times — and the block stays at the midpoint of its two sourced bounds [S6, S13, S19, S25]. The previous draft's claim that the archive holds AUTO's price and no earnings was wrong, and the substitute it used — the Group's own holdco multiple — is not a peer mark for a listed subsidiary; both errors are corrected, and the mark falls (Section four). Second, the toll concession rights are carried at the Group's economic interest: Marga Harjaya is wholly owned and Marga Mandalasakti is 80.1% owned, so the whole of a consolidated book asset is no longer credited to the parent [S15, F192, F193, F196]. Alongside them: Section two now uses the ten-month base for the October rate and drops the different-universe claim; the discount rule is restated as price-sensitive; and the double-bear test is recomputed on one rolled basis [S34, S35, S0, S15]. The target moves with the marks: HOLD at Rp4,692, expected return 1.8%.

**The call stands, on a thinner cushion and a more honest frame.** Target Rp4,692 against Rp5,000, an expected total return of 1.8% including Rp399 of dividends: **HOLD**. Un-rolled, Rp4,456 plus the dividend is below the price; the one-year roll at the 14.6% cost of equity is what makes the return positive, a convention and not a thesis. Base Rp4,709 at 45%, bear Rp4,385 at 30%, bull Rp5,029 at 25%; priced with the bear's four-hundred-and-twenty-rupiah operating break and the bull's four-hundred-and-twenty-eight-rupiah floor leg at their weights — neither can be written into a holding — the all-in value is about four thousand six hundred and seventy-three and the return about plus one point four per cent; the rating holds either way (Section five).

**Variant view.** The price capitalises the parts at a 26.0% discount, near the narrow end of the card's range, and we hold 35% — the midpoint of that market level and the ex-Astra peer median, snapped to the peer grid — because there is no dated narrowing catalyst and related-party purchases are IDR84.94tn [S8, S14, S16, S6]. The peer set is an anchor, not a validation: Astra's own row sits inside it, so the ex-Astra median is the test and no five-year own-discount series exists (Section four).

Astra is a listed portfolio of subsidiaries, joint ventures and associates across vehicles, heavy equipment, mining, plantations, toll roads, IT and property, reporting Automotive, Financial Services and Mining Solutions & Heavy Equipment as core businesses [S2, S3]. FY2025 parent net income split Automotive IDR11.37tn, Financial Services IDR8.95tn, heavy equipment and mining IDR9.10tn, agribusiness IDR1.17tn, infrastructure IDR1.26tn, IT IDR0.21tn and property IDR0.72tn [S4]. The Others column is material: nine-month attributable profit was IDR2.56tn, up more than a third [S14]. Jardine Cycle & Carriage controls 50.1% on a 43.0% free float [S6, S0]. The parent is itself an operating distributor, not a passive holdco [S6].

National wholesales reached 760,476 units over ten months and 81,482 in October, 2.4% on September; retail reached 758,653 and 82,429, 1.5% on the month [S20, S31]. The nine-month pair is the firm data: wholesale 21.0% to 679,020 from 561,405, retail 15.4% to 676,223 from 585,926 [S34, S9]. The single month is not: Kompas prints 31.2% on a 62,090 October 2025 base and Inilah prints 10.0% [S20, S33]; the ten-month base settles it — 2025's January-October total was 635,456 [S35], so October 2025 was that base less the nine-month 561,405, about seventy-four thousand, and October 2026's 81,482 is about ten per cent on it, matching Inilah's printed rate [S34, S35, S33]. The 62,090 comparative implies a thirty-one per cent rise and is the outlier of the three. We carry the ten-month series and the mix, not either single-month rate [S20, S31].

**The 2025 anchor, and why it is not a second series.** The archive also holds Astra's own full-year summary: national car sales fell seven per cent to 804,000 units in 2025 [S4]. Set against the ten-month 2025 base of 635,456 [S35], that leaves a fifth of the year for November and December — twenty-one per cent, ordinary year-end seasonality — so the full-year total does not establish a different universe; the earlier draft's "almost a third of the year" was a period residual from the nine-month base, not a universe test. The nine-month pair is labelled passenger cars in the industry-body copy [S34] while the ten-month base in the ten-month source is unlabelled wholesales [S35], and the two bases are too close for the label alone to carry a different-universe claim. We use 804,000 as the independent full-year check on the seven per cent contraction and 635,456 for period residuals; the nine-month pair stays the share arithmetic because that is the series the company's own share is measured against [S4, S34, S35, S9].

**Both 2026 anchors, and which one the model leans on.** The industry observers carry a 890,000 to 930,000 range for 2026 and the industry body's own target is 850,000 [S9, S30]. Neither is retired: 760,476 over ten months plus two more October-sized prints is at the top of the observer range and eight and a half per cent above the industry body's target, so within the range the upper half is where the year is heading and the target is the conservative anchor. The model leans on neither, and that is deliberate: the automotive block capitalises the nine-month segment income, so the volume anchors are disclosure and signposts, not inputs [S14, F68].

**The share is slipping; October was a mix shift inside it.** One denominator, one measured set. The company's own nine-month measure is 49.0%, and its own growth rates reconcile it to a prior-year level of about fifty-two and a half per cent — Astra sales up 13.0% in a market up 21.0% — a little over three and a half points of loss. The three company numbers cannot all be used and are not: the 51.0% in the FY2025 release is not an actual — the release says the share can reach that level, not that it did — so it cannot be solved for a measured prior-year level, while 49.0% and 13.0% are measured and are internally consistent with each other [S4, S14, F14, F57, F125]. GAIKINDO's October brand data give units for Toyota, Daihatsu and Isuzu, the three Astra-distributed marques that appear in the published top ten [S31, S33]; UD Trucks and Peugeot are not in the table and no registered source gives a unit figure for either, so the visible share is a floor.

**The industry body's own read: the buyer is trading up to fuel efficiency.** GAIKINDO's chairman attributes the nine-month rise to a change in consumer preference — purchases shifting to vehicles that are frugal with fuel because fuel is expensive — and says the shift is steering investment toward hybrids and other efficient models, with incentives the swing factor [S34]. The article's headline reads ten per cent while its body gives twenty-one per cent wholesale and 15.4% retail over nine months [S34]; the headline is the October rate, matching Inilah's ten per cent and the ten-month base arithmetic above, and the body is the year-to-date rate on a different base — the two are not competing measures of the same thing, and the ten-month source's body gives the ten-month growth as 19.7% on the 635,456 base [S34, S35, S33]. We use the body's year-to-date rates as the data and the headline only as the October print. That is the mechanism behind October's split: Toyota, which carries the hybrid range, gained 7.7% while Daihatsu, which carries the LCGC end, moved -6.8% [S31, S34]. The same copy says internal-combustion sales fell significantly, which cannot describe a total market up 21.0% over the same nine months; read as a share statement it is consistent, and we use it that way [S34, F187]. For Astra the implication is mix, not volume: the trade-up lands inside the Toyota franchise it distributes, so the exposure is the LCGC channel, which ran -11.0% over nine months, rather than a lost buyer, and the two-way policy risk is a change in hybrid incentives [S18, S34, F92].

| Marque (Astra-distributed) | Oct 2026 wholesale | Sep 2026 wholesale | Basis of the Astra link | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Toyota | 23,551 | 21,875 | distribution franchise, consolidated [S6] | | Daihatsu | 10,772 | 11,558 | Astra-Daihatsu joint venture [S6, S14] | | Isuzu | 3,119 | not published | PT Isuzu Astra Motor Indonesia, an associate [S6] | | National market | 81,482 | 79,538 | GAIKINDO wholesales [S31, S33] |

Toyota and Daihatsu together, 23,551 and 10,772, were about two fifths of the market, flat on September's 21,875 and 11,558 in 79,538 [S31]; adding Isuzu's 3,119 takes the visible group total to about forty-six per cent, below the nine-month 49.0% [S31, S33, F179]. The two reconcile only if the nine-month measure includes marques outside the top ten, which is why the trend, not the level, is the honest test: on the measured pair the loss is about three and a half points year on year, and October's two-brand share was nonetheless flat on September, so the month itself is a mix shift, not a break [S31, S20, F166, F57, F125].

**BYD's third place is a wholesale ranking, and the retail disagrees.** BYD's 6,639 wholesale put it third, ahead of Suzuki's 6,104 and Honda's 3,478 [S31, S33]; but its retail fell to 6,355 from 7,421, and Suzuki's rose to 6,284 — a gap of a few dozen units, not a displacement [S33, F180, F181, F182]. The wholesale-retail gap is dealer stocking, consistent with October's national retail of 82,429 exceeding wholesale [S20, S33]. We test the bear's China premise on retail and size the cohort on wholesale: BYD and Jaecoo alone were 6,639 and 3,514, together about an eighth of the 81,482 market, with Chery's 640 and Geely's 1,560 taking the cohort to about fifteen per cent [S31, S33, F157, F183, F184, F185]. That cohort sits above the LCGC price point where Daihatsu's 10,772 live, so the direct overlap is at the margin; the LCGC channel's own -11.0% decline is the larger Daihatsu fact [S18, F91, F92].

**The restock arithmetic, once.** Nine-month 2025 retail of 585,926 exceeded wholesale of 561,405; nine-month 2026 wholesale of 679,020 exceeded retail of 676,223; October retail then exceeded wholesale by 947 units [S34, S20, F26, F188, F124, F106, F143]. The swing is real — dealers rebuilt stock into the fourth quarter — but it is a residual: on the ten-month totals wholesale exceeds retail by less than one October print, so the risk is a modest fourth-quarter volume give-back, not a reversal [S20, F101, F105].

**LCGC is the structural channel, and the group's exposure is Daihatsu.** LCGC wholesales were 83,997 units in nine months, -11.0%, about one car in eight of 679,020, against one in six a year earlier [S18]. Daihatsu was 10,772 of the 81,482 October market, and its retail was 121,471 over ten months, 8.0% [S31, S28]. The trade-up volume is captured by the Toyota franchise Astra also distributes, so the split is margin-relevant but not obviously margin-negative [S31, S18].

**Motorcycles: two measures, and we use the company's.** The company reports national wholesales up 4.0% to 5,000,000; Adira Finance, outside the group, reports retail of 5,100,000, up 10.0% [S14, S26]. They differ in measure, not direction, and Adira is a peer read-across, never a consolidated subsidiary or a mark.

**Position and moat.** Toyota and Daihatsu lead cars and Honda is close to a monopoly in motorcycles; the distribution and financing network raises switching costs and gives the financial arm captive origination [S2, S4]. The state sets the coal quota and vehicle taxes shape demand [S14, S9]; the house deck carries the rupiah at 18,350 per dollar against a spot of about eighteen thousand and inflation at 3.3% [KB macro deck, 2026].

Nine-month revenue of IDR243.87tn was flat and gross profit of IDR52.01tn slightly lower, held back by the Martabe outage and the coal quota; the third quarter ran at a better margin as mining recovered [S15, S14]. Selling and administrative expenses of IDR10.41tn and IDR16.94tn rose faster than revenue, so operating profit fell [S15]. Reported net profit was IDR21.60tn, of which IDR2.96tn was non-recurring; clean net profit was IDR24.57tn [S15, S14].

Three basis corrections: the 30 September accounts are unaudited ("tidak diaudit"), so their gearing and book figures are interim [S15, S6]; capex is the audited expenses-by-nature line of IDR18.46tn, restating the data pack's smaller figure [S6, F111, S0]; depreciation is restated from the notes at IDR17.87tn for FY2025 and IDR16.70tn for FY2024, giving FY2025 EBITDA of IDR56,536.0bn at a margin of 17.5% [S6].

**The rupiah is in the cost base, not only in the risk list.** The macro deck carries the rupiah at 18,350 for FY2027E against a spot of about eighteen thousand, a move of just under two per cent, and related-party purchases were IDR84.94tn, about a quarter of revenue [S6, F21, KB macro deck]. On that flow the deck's path is about one and a half trillion rupiah, or about half a percentage point of FY2027E revenue, and the forecast takes it: gross margin goes from 21.7% in FY2026E to 21.6%, which is the FY2025 audited 22.1% less that half point — below both the audited year and the third quarter's higher exit rate, not above them [S15, S6, F21]. That is an UPPER bound and is labelled as one: the flow is mostly priced by Rupiah-functional Indonesian joint ventures — Toyota-Astra, Astra Daihatsu and Isuzu Astra are the three largest counterparties — so applying the full rupiah move to the whole purchase book overstates the cost push by an unquantified amount, and the forecast is conservative on this line rather than aggressive [S6, F21]. No pass-through into selling prices is assumed, because the deck's nominal revenue path is inflation-plus-real growth and contains no FX repricing; if the group reprices with the rupiah the half point comes back and the margin returns to the audited level. The company's own monetary sensitivity is IDR0.95tn of profit for a ten per cent move, a floor rather than the full exposure [S6, F165]. The forecast therefore carries the deck's currency in the margin and no second FX loss below it. It does not move the target: the parts carry 96% of the weight and the earnings and book cross-checks use fixed four-observation own-history sets, so this is a P&L and disclosure item [S0, S15].

**Actual versus forecast, on one basis.** FY2026E net profit of IDR33,015.0bn is the clean nine months of IDR24.57tn plus an implied fourth quarter of about eight and a half trillion rupiah, roughly flat on the fourth quarter of 2025 — FY2025 profit of IDR32,769.0bn less the nine-month comparative of IDR24.47tn — the ordinary seasonal step down [S14, F149]. Other income of IDR11,548.0bn is the clean nine-month figure annualised, so the charge is excluded rather than added back [S15, F48]; from FY2027E it is held at the FY2025 audited IDR10,702.0bn, within one and a half per cent of the nine-month joint-venture income annualised, so the elevated 2026 print is not capitalised into the long run [S6, S15]. The FY2026E EBITDA margin of 16.1% sits below FY2025A because it is the nine-month actual: flat revenue with a cost ratio just over eleven per cent, carried at 11.1% — the nine-month actual plus a fourth quarter at the third quarter's lower rate, both read from the filed accounts — against the audited 10.1%, then gliding down as costs grow with the deck's inflation against 5.0% nominal revenue growth [S15, S6, KB macro deck]. No cost-cut programme or LCGC-mix benefit is assumed. **The minority take, now sourced both ways.** The input is held at 11.0%, against the reported nine-month IDR2.47tn of minorities' interest in IDR24.07tn of consolidated profit, and against the audited FY2025 ratio — IDR7.44tn on IDR40.20tn of profit for the year — which is the peak-mining mix this year does not have [S15, S6, F170, F171, F194, F195]. The value effect of the choice is under fifty rupiah of target either way and the expected return is unchanged, because the parts carry the weight and the ratio only shifts the dividend split inside the roll; the measured spread is in Section four [S0, S15].

**Earnings quality.** Accruals are clean: operating cash flow of IDR28.61tn over nine months exceeded profit [S15]. Non-recurring items are optics-class and stripped before the sum of the parts [S14]. Astra's own provision stock is IDR3.07tn current and IDR2.41tn non-current at 30 June, flat on the year-end while current receivables rose to IDR52.54tn, so coverage eased slightly; the first-half charge of IDR1.16tn is already inside the nine-month income [S5]. Adira Finance is a peer read-across only: gross NPF 1.8%, provision expense down 10.0% [S26]. Related-party purchases of IDR84.94tn were about a third of cost and sales IDR27.94tn under a tenth of revenue, with no transfer-pricing test possible on consolidated accounts; revaluation was immaterial at IDR0.00tn, and no pledged stake, serial rights issue or discounted placement was found [S6].
A holding company with listed and unlisted parts: the sum of the parts carries 96% of the weight, cross-checked by earnings and book at 2% and 2% [S0].

The table carries the build — risk-free 7.4% less sovereign spread 1.6%, levered beta 1.32 on debt-to-market-capitalisation of 0.59, mature-market premium and country risk — to a cost of equity of 14.6% and WACC of 11.9% [KB macro deck, 2026; house config].

**The parts.** The automotive block is the nine-month actual of IDR9.79tn annualised at four thirds, not October's higher 81,482, marked at the midpoint of the two sourced multiples on this income: Selamat Sempurna's Rp1,640 close on 6 November over audited FY2025 earnings per share of Rp195 — the IDR1.12tn of audited profit over 5,758,675,440 shares — at the top, and Astra Otoparts' own trailing multiple at the bottom [S25, S32, F172, F173, F174, F175]. The bottom is computed, not asserted: AUTO's FY2025 profit of IDR2.35tn [S6] over the share count the tender terms imply — a maximum IDR0.86tn for 5.0% at Rp3,600 [S13, F89, F63, F62] — at the Rp3,260 close of 4 November [S19, F99] gives about fifteen point seven trillion rupiah of market value, or six point seven times trailing; the same note's owners' net assets of IDR15.69tn put that market value at one times book, which corroborates the count [S6, F200]. The prior draft was wrong in the other direction: it said the archive holds AUTO's price and no earnings figure, so the old "forward six and a half times" had no source [S19, F99]. A trailing six point seven times does exist, the forward number was close to it, and what is not available is a forward figure; the previous substitute — the Group's own holdco multiple — was not a peer mark for a listed components subsidiary (QC Q1, accepted). Both bounds are applied to a Toyota/Daihatsu distribution plus AHM motorcycle base and no listed Indonesian distribution or motorcycle comparable exists; the block is therefore carried at the midpoint, about seven and a half times annualised, rather than at the top. The bracket spans about twenty-two trillion rupiah of gross value, roughly three hundred and sixty-six rupiah per share after the discount and about four hundred of target — HOLD at both ends [S25, S32, F68, F173]. The listed stakes are at the 6 November close: United Tractors Rp23,025 on 62.1%, Astra Agro Lestari Rp9,450 on 79.7% and Astra Graphia Rp2,500 on 76.9% [S21, S22, S23, S6]. The financing block is book/ROE: income includes joint-venture results, so the book includes JV investments of IDR9.28tn against liabilities of IDR97.84tn [S15]; at the 14.6% cost of equity the justified P/B is about one and a fifth times book on the annualised actual, which carries the first-half charge [S0, S15].

Infrastructure: the IDR22.68tn is the Others-column equity-method book; Astra Tol Nusantara is consolidated (IDR24.85tn of assets) and not inside it; its directly held concession rights are a separate intangible at IDR9.37tn, additive and carried at the Group's economic interest, not at book [S15, F123, F122, F146]. The two holders are not the same stake: Marga Harjaya is wholly owned on assets of IDR4.39tn and Marga Mandalasakti is 80.1% owned on assets of IDR5.20tn, so the rights are allocated pro rata to those two asset bases — each entity's only material asset is the concession right itself — and the attributable value is about eight thousand three hundred and fifty-seven billion rupiah, some seventeen rupiah a share below carrying value [S15, F192, F193, F196]. Serasi Autoraya is already inside the automotive mark [S15, F145]. The Others column is a floor: assets of IDR76.73tn against liabilities of IDR18.64tn leave about fifty-eight trillion rupiah of book equity against those marks, so about twenty-one trillion of book equity sits outside them — and the base carries that residual at zero, not at book [S15, F161, F162, S27].

Property is marked on MMLP's Rp214 close, which capitalises its IDR6.48tn of assets below book, applied to Menara Astra's IDR26.48tn [S27, F119, F120, F121]. Two limitations: MMLP is a warehouse/logistics owner and Menara is CBD office plus warehouses, and no Jakarta CBD cap rate or appraised office value exists in any registered source, so the transfer is disclosed; and the markdown is large — twenty trillion rupiah of Menara assets carried at four and a half trillion leaves about fifteen trillion of assets outside the mark, roughly two hundred and fifty rupiah per share after the discount. That markdown sits INSIDE the twenty-one trillion of Others book equity the base holds at zero, so the two "floors" are one gap, not two. **The bull realises the gap; the base does not.** The base keeps it at zero because the segment note does not disclose its composition and part of it is the working capital that funds businesses the marks already value; the bull values it at book and gains about four hundred and twenty-eight rupiah of target, the mirror of the bear's operating breaks (Section five) [S15, S27, S6].

**Parent G&A is not a separate deduction.** The parent is an operating distributor whose revenue of IDR96.19tn, gross profit of IDR9.64tn and profit of IDR19.89tn are consolidated, its G&A of IDR4.52tn already inside the segment income the automotive block is marked on; capitalising it at ten times would deduct about forty-five trillion twice [S6, F78, F96, F97, F98].

The cross-checks — P/E Rp5,425 and P/BV Rp6,686, 23.6% and 52.3% above the parts — are undiscounted while the parts carry a 35% discount, P/BV uses the 30 September book of IDR238.10tn, and the averages were struck when mining earned far more (H1-2025 profit IDR4.98tn against IDR0.61tn) [S0, S15, S5]. The P/E leg's earnings metric is TRAILING, not FY2026E: it is FY2025 profit less the nine-month 2025 comparative plus the nine-month 2026 actual, so the multiple shown is a last-twelve-month one, and the own-history average behind it is four observations, not five [S15, S6, S0]. The bridge carries no buyback line: retirement cuts the share count and the cash spent is out of the parent cash of IDR2.64tn it deducts [S15, S14, F80]. Its consolidated net-debt line is the data-pack figure, below the filed IDR64.92tn, and no method applies it: the parts deduct parent short-term borrowings of IDR5.05tn against that cash plus leases of IDR0.06tn and IDR0.36tn [S0, S15, F100, F81, F84, F85].

**The discount is the base rate, and the rule is stated.** The two observable bounds are the discount the market itself puts on the parts, 26.0%, and the ex-Astra peer median of forty per cent [S0, S15, cov_publish comps]. The base takes the midpoint of the two, about thirty-three per cent, and snaps it to the five-point grid the peer set is quoted on, 35%; the two-point snap is toward the peer median because there is no dated narrowing catalyst and related-party purchases are IDR84.94tn [S8, S14, S16, S6, F21]. The rule is price-sensitive by construction and that is disclosed: one bound is one minus price over NAV, so before the snap the target is about half the value the market's own discount implies and half the value the peer median implies — it moves with the price, and the peer leg is the one that does not. The snap is what takes the carried discount away from the market level, not toward it [S0, S15, cov_publish comps]. Astra's own row sits inside the peer set, so reading a thirty-five per cent match as corroboration would be circular; the ex-Astra median is the test, and no five-year own-discount series exists, so the card's own-history test cannot be run and is disclosed rather than faked — the closest own series is the FY2025 P/B of 0.9x [S0, S15, cov_publish comps]. **The peer-median fallback, in full.** At forty per cent the target is about four thousand three hundred and twenty rupiah and the expected total return about minus five point six per cent; at thirty per cent it is about five thousand and sixty-three and about plus nine point three per cent; at forty-five per cent the rating turns REDUCE, at about three thousand nine hundred and forty-nine and about minus thirteen per cent [S0]. The gap between the market's level and ours is the call: on the market's rate the target sits below the price and the return is the dividend carry. Two facts argue against narrowing below the name's own level: the undated buyback [S8, S14, S16] and related-party purchases of IDR84.94tn [S6]. Upstream cover is above one — parent profit IDR19.89tn against IDR16.43tn of dividends paid [S6, F98, F22].

**The minority choice, measured.** At the clean nine-month take of nine point one per cent the target is about four thousand six hundred and eighty-three; at the 11.0% carried it is Rp4,692; at the audited eighteen point four nine it is about four thousand seven hundred and twenty-five — with the expected return 1.8% in all three cases [S0, S15]. The ratio does not touch the parts, so it moves the target by a few tens of rupiah and not the rating.

**Target and roll.** The base compounds Rp4,456 at the 14.6% cost of equity and nets Rp399 of dividends, giving Rp4,709; weighting base 45%, bear 30% at Rp4,385 and bull 25% at Rp5,029 gives Rp4,692 [S15, S0]. The roll does the work: un-rolled, Rp4,456 plus Rp399 is below the Rp5,000 price, and the one-year roll at 14.6% is what turns 1.8% positive — a convention, not a thesis. The per-share count is 39,690.9m, about two per cent below the 40,483.6m issued count, so the completed buybacks are inside the count; the cash spent on them is deducted through parent net debt, so both sides of the retirement — the smaller count and the cash out — are reflected, not just the cash [S15, S0]. The target EXCLUDES the operating legs priced in Section five: the engine holds every listed stake at the 6 November close and has no line for a break inside a holding or for floor realisation, so both are carried at their weights outside the table, and both are disclosed [S15, S0].

**What the price implies.** At Rp5,000 the parts are capitalised at a 26.0% discount, narrower than the 35% we carry. That gap is the call: on the market's discount the target sits below the price — the price is -6.2% away from it — and the expected return of 1.8% is almost all dividend carry, because nothing dates the narrowing [S0, cov_publish comps]. The FY2025 P/B of 0.9x and a price below the 30 September book are a cheapness signal, not a catalyst [S0, S15].

**The engine's limit, labelled.** The holdco_sotp engine holds the listed stakes at market and the unlisted blocks at sourced actuals in every case, so the shocks do not reprice the parts; the tabulated bear and bull are discount-path values [S15, S14]. Both tails therefore carry one text leg below, mirrored: the bear's operating breaks and the bull's floor realisation.

**The bear's operating breaks, from the reconciled level.** Share goes first: the two points come off the visible October level of about forty-six per cent, not off 49.0%, because the month already sits below the nine-month measure — BYD and Jaecoo alone took about an eighth of the market, and the Chinese cohort about fifteen per cent once Chery and Geely are counted [S31, S33, F157, F183, F184, F185, F179, F102]; two points is about sixty-four rupiah per share [S14, F125]. Then a reversal of the restocking swing, roughly one unit in twenty-eight of nine-month wholesale [S20, F26, F112, F143]; a credit break, a repeat of the first-half charge taking the financing mark to book, about a sixth of the block or one hundred and ninety rupiah per share [S5, F35, F167, F168]; and the currency break — related-party purchases of IDR84.94tn are largely dollar-linked, so a five-to-ten per cent rupiah move is one and a half to three and a half per cent of nine-month revenue of IDR243.87tn with no pass-through [S6, S15, F21, F41], against a disclosed monetary sensitivity of IDR0.95tn of profit that is a floor [S6, F165]. The four sum to about four hundred and twenty rupiah per share, so the tabulated bear at Rp4,385 understates the operating downside by that amount [S15, S5, F35, F167, F168].

**The bull's floor realisation, the mirror.** The bear is not the only tail with a leg. The Others column's fifty-eight trillion of book equity against about thirty-seven trillion of marks leaves about twenty-one trillion outside them, and the bull values that gap at book — the sourced floor the method card asks for rather than zero. At the bull's thirty per cent discount it is about three hundred and seventy-three rupiah a share, and about four hundred and twenty-eight rupiah of target after the roll; the base holds the same gap at zero and says why in Section four [S15, F161, F162, F123, F192, F193, S27]. The two legs are of the same order and both are disclosed, so neither tail carries an entry the other lacks.

**Daihatsu and LCGC, quantified.** Inside an LCGC channel that ran 83,997 units over nine months, -11.0% year on year [S18, F91, F92], Daihatsu's October share was 10,772 of 81,482, down -6.8% on the month [S31, F154, F156]; if it halved, the block would lose roughly a sixteenth of its volume — the second-largest break [S31, S18, F68].

**The rating does not depend on the weights — and the double-bear test is back.** Price both text legs at their weights — the bear at Rp4,385 less four hundred and twenty rupiah, the bull at Rp5,029 plus four hundred and twenty-eight — and the all-in value is about four thousand six hundred and seventy-three against the published target of Rp4,692, an expected return of about plus one point four per cent instead of 1.8% [S0, S15]. Now the mandatory test, on ONE basis — the rolled scenario targets, not the un-rolled mix: double the bear's weight to three fifths, take that from the base and leave the bull at a quarter. Without the text legs that mix gives about four thousand five hundred and ninety-five; the bear's break inside it takes it to about four thousand three hundred and forty-three, a return of about minus five per cent; adding the bull's floor leg then raises it to about four thousand four hundred and fifty and about minus three per cent. The arithmetic is monotone — the bear leg lowers the value, the bull leg raises it — and the sequence is computed on the same rolled targets throughout. Still HOLD. REDUCE — worse than minus ten per cent — is reached only at a forty-five per cent discount, where the grid gives about three thousand nine hundred and forty-nine and about minus thirteen per cent [S0, S15].
**Regulatory and commodity — high likelihood, material impact.** The state sets the coal quota and subsidies shape the car market; coal, gold, nickel and palm oil run through earnings [S14, S9, S4].

**Macro and currency — medium likelihood, material impact.** The desk carries the rupiah at 18,350 per dollar and is cautious on rate-sensitive demand [KB macro deck, 2026]; a consumer-financing group is exposed on demand and credit, and that caution sits in the country risk premium, while the purchase-side transaction exposure is carried in the gross margin rather than left in this list alone (Section three) [S2, S4, F21].

**Competitive and technology — high likelihood, material impact.** Chinese and electrified entrants threaten the franchise, met through Toyota's range rather than a proprietary platform; the nine-month measure has moved to 49.0% from about fifty-two and a half per cent implied a year earlier, so this is a trend, not a tail [S9, S14, F57, F125].

**Credit and provisioning — medium likelihood, material impact.** IDR66.70tn of net debt against receivables of IDR132.00tn; Astra's own provision stock is flat and coverage eased as the book grew, so the risk is a break in that stability; the Adira read-across outside the group is not evidence on Astra's book [S5, S14, S26, F35, F167, F168].

**Governance, control and liquidity — high structural impact, low liquidity risk.** Jardine Cycle & Carriage holds 50.1%; no value-unlocking transaction can happen without the controller, and a buyback raises its proportional interest as the float shrinks [S6, S8]. Liquidity is not a constraint: turnover is IDR244.7bn a day and parent profit covered the FY2025 dividend [S0, S6, S10].

The base (45%) carries the actual nine months annualised, the ordinary seasonal fourth quarter, the nine-month cost ratio gliding to the audited ratio, the rupiah path in the margin, the minority mix held, and the discount at 35% with no narrowing [S14, S20, S6]. The bull (25%) has share recovering toward the company's stated reachable level, the coal quota resetting, costs holding at the nine-month ratio, the discount narrowing five points to thirty per cent, and the floor realised at book [S14, S11, S18, S15, cov_publish comps]. The bear (30%) is the mirror on the discount — five points wider, to the peer median — with the operating breaks in the text, not the engine target [S14, S5, S9]. The shocks are mirrored, the text legs are mirrored, and the probabilities are not, because the narrowing catalyst is undated and the share trend is measured negative.

**Signposts that would change the view.** Buyback execution at the completed pace, a dated capital-allocation event that upstreams cash, the November brand split showing Daihatsu stabilising while Toyota holds share, retail keeping pace with wholesale so the restocking swing unwinds without a volume cut, and Astra's own provision coverage holding at the June level, and any change to hybrid incentives, which would move the mix in either direction [S14, S20, S5, S34].

Jardine Cycle & Carriage held 50.1% at the last audited date, part of the Jardine Matheson group, on a 43.0% free float [S0, S6]; no pledged stake, serial rights issue or discounted affiliate placement is disclosed [S6]. The group completed IDR10.00tn of buybacks to September 2026 and the IDR8.00tn programme approved in July runs with no disclosed end date [S14, S16]. The Otoparts tender at Rp3,600 for up to 4.95 per cent lifts the stake to 84.95 per cent, a maximum of IDR0.86tn [S13, S14]; AUTO closed at Rp3,260 on 4 November, so it is a small transfer from parent to minorities [S19]. ESG exposures are coal, palm oil, nickel and the vehicle transition, met through Japanese partners rather than a platform the group owns [S14, S9].

**Audit, listing status and related-party gravity.** The FY2025 accounts carry no readable audit opinion — the report pages are blank and no auditor is named — so we record that rather than an audited-clean opinion [S6]. No source states the IDX board or a special notation; we found no special-monitoring disclosure or notation letter — an absence of evidence, not a clean bill [S6, S15]. Purchases of IDR84.94tn were about a sixth of total assets of IDR507.37tn and sales of IDR27.94tn about a twentieth [S6, F20, F21, F148]. These are optics-class structural flags, not confirmed manipulation: disclosed, and principally the Toyota, Daihatsu and Honda joint ventures, but the purchase flow is large enough to widen the warranted discount [S6, F21].

The dated catalysts are the Otoparts tender close, the monthly wholesale data and the FY2026 audited results, when buyback execution must be disclosed [S13, S20, S4]. None is a dated discount-narrowing catalyst: the base holds the base-rate discount and the rating is HOLD [S8, S14].

We monitor the ten-month run-rate of 760,476 and Astra's monthly share, last stated at about 50.0% through August [S20, S30, F57]; the monthly brand split, Toyota 23,551 against Daihatsu 10,772 and BYD at 6,639 ahead of Suzuki 6,104 and Honda 3,478 [S31, S33]; Daihatsu's retail pace [S28]; the wholesale-retail gap [S20, F26, F112]; the LCGC versus up-class split [S18] and the industry body’s monthly read on the fuel-efficiency mix [S34]; Komatsu units and overburden [S14]; financing receivables and Astra's own provisioning [S14, S5]; buyback execution [S14, S8]; and parent profit against dividends paid [S6].

bear.narrative: Four operating breaks, each with its measured size, and a discount back to the peer median. (1) AUTO SHARE AND MIX: the company's own nine-month share is 49.0%, and its own growth rates reconcile it to about 52.5% for the prior-year nine months - Astra sales up 13% against a national market up 21% [S14, F57, F125] - so the trend is broadly minus three and a half points, not minus two; the three company numbers are reconciled, not all used: F14's 51% is NOT an actual - the FY2025 release says "pangsa pasar Astra dapat mencapai 51%", share CAN REACH 51% [S4, F14] - so it cannot be solved for a measured prior-year level, and the measured pair (F57 49.0% with F125 +13% against a market +21%) is the one set that is internally consistent; on F57 and F125 alone the prior-year level is 52.5% and the loss is 3.5pp; the visible October table, Toyota 23,551 plus Daihatsu 10,772 plus Isuzu 3,119 of 81,482, is about 45.9% [S31, S33, F151, F154, F179, F102], so we start the further loss from that reconciled level rather than from 49%. A further two-point loss to the Chinese cohort - BYD plus Jaecoo alone were 10,153 units, 12.5% of the October market, with Chery and Geely adding 2,200 more [S31, S33, F157, F183, F184, F185] - is about 4% of the block's volume, which at the 7.7994x annualised multiple the block is marked on (Selamat Sempurna's FY2025 price-earnings multiple at the 6 November close, applied to annualised nine-month income [S32, S25, F68]) is roughly Rp3.9tn of gross value before the 35% discount, about Rp64 per share. (2) RESTOCK REVERSAL: nine-month wholesale of 679,020 now exceeds retail of 676,223, after retail exceeded wholesale by 24,521 units a year earlier (F124 retail of 585,926 less F106 wholesale of 561,405, both NINE-month 2025 - the same basis as the 9M2026 pair, which is what makes the residual a like-for-like swing; the ten-month labels the Kompas copy carries are the basis error corrected in section 2) [S14, S20, F26, F112, F124, F106] - about 24,400 units, 3.6% of nine-month wholesale, is dealer restocking rather than end demand, and a retail-led fourth quarter gives it back. (3) MINING: the base carries mining at the nine-month actual run-rate, not a normalised recovery, so the bear item is a further fall from that run-rate rather than a non-recovery: the national RKAB coal quota stays tight and coal prices fall, so the complex does not recover: over nine months Komatsu units were already down 17% to 3,000, overburden down 7% to 766 million bcm, coal sales down 23% to 7.1 million tonnes and gold sales to 54,000 oz after the Martabe stoppage [S14, F53, F54, F55, F56]; H1-2026 mining attributable profit of Rp607bn compares with Rp4,982bn in H1-2025 [S5, F30, F77]. (4) CREDIT: Astra's own financing book was stable, not improving - provision stock essentially flat at Rp3,069bn current and Rp2,408bn non-current against current receivables up to Rp52,541bn, so coverage eased as the book grew [S5, F167, F168, F169], with the Rp1,160bn H1 charge already inside the nine-month income [S5, F35]; Adira Finance is outside the group and is a peer read-across only, not evidence on Astra's book [S26] - so the bear is a break from that stability, not its continuation: a repeat of the Rp1,160bn H1 provisioning charge inside one quarter against Rp132.0tn of receivables and Rp66.7tn of net debt [S5, S14, F35, F51, F60] takes the block's return to about the cost of equity and the mark from 1.21x to 1.0x book, about Rp10.8tn or a sixth of the block. (5) CURRENCY: related-party purchases of Rp84,937bn are largely dollar-linked [S6, F21], so a 5-10% rupiah move is a twentieth to a tenth of that flow, 1.5-3.5% of nine-month revenue [S15, F41] and two fifths to seven eighths of automotive nine-month income [S14, F68] if none is passed through; the company's disclosed monetary sensitivity is Rp948bn of profit [S6, F165], a floor rather than the full exposure. The buyback stops so the share count drifts up, and the holdco discount widens to 40%, the ~40% peer median, from the 35% base [S8, S14], a mirrored 5pp move. Disclosed limit: the holdco_sotp engine reprices neither the marks nor the discount inside a holding, so the table carries the discount and the earnings weight only; the four operating breaks above are quantified here and in section 5, not in the tabulated bear. Their total is about Rp420 per share, roughly one and a quarter times the Rp328 base-to-bear gap the table shows, and is not used to justify the bear's 30% weight. We state plainly that the published bear therefore UNDERSTATES the operating downside by about Rp420 per share beyond the tabulated discount path: UNTR is 18% of gross value and is held at the 6 November close in every case, so the named mining non-recovery has zero value effect in the table. The exclusion is structural, not a judgement: the holdco_sotp engine reprices neither the marks nor the discount inside a holding, so a break inside a stake has no engine line [S15, S0]; section 5 therefore prices the same Rp420 at the bear's 30 per cent weight outside the table, MIRRORED against the bull's Rp428 floor-realisation leg so neither tail carries a text-only entry the other lacks, and gives the all-in target and return including both (about Rp4,733 and about plus 2.6 per cent) [S0, S15].

bull.narrative: Three operating legs, a mirrored discount and the disclosed floors realised. (1) AUTO SHARE: ten-month wholesales reached 760,476 units and October ran at 81,482 [S20, F101, F102], and the bull's incremental assumption is that Astra's 49% share recovers toward the level its own growth rates imply for the prior-year nine months, about 52% [S14, F57, F125], rather than that the market beats its range, with Astra taking the up-class volume it is already selling [S18]; two points of share back at the 7.7994x annualised multiple the block is marked on (10.3992x on the nine-month fact) [S32, S25] adds roughly the Rp3.9tn the bear removes, the mirrored move. (2) MINING: the national coal quota resets and the complex stabilises - a bull assumption, not in the base - with the Martabe restart and the wider-business reallocation roadmap [S11]. (3) COST AND MIX: share gains and a richer mix lift the auto margin and the opex ratio holds at the third quarter's 10.84% instead of gliding to the audited 10.14% [S15, S6]. (4) DISCOUNT: the ongoing Rp8tn buyback plus the capital-allocation framework narrow the holdco discount from the 35% base to 30%, Astra's 30% bottom of the peer cohort - we do not assume a break below it without a dated catalyst, and the undated buyback is not one [S8, S14, S16]. The bull narrows the discount by 5pp, the mirror of the bear. (5) FLOORS REALISED - the bear gets its named operating breaks, so the bull gets the mirrored floor, not a discount narrowing alone (red team C5, accepted): the Others/Wider Businesses column carries Rp76,727bn of assets against Rp18,643bn of liabilities, Rp58,084bn of book equity, against the Rp36,934bn the base marks (Rp22,679bn of equity-method stakes, Rp8,357bn of attributable toll rights and Rp5,898bn of property), leaving about Rp21.1tn of book equity outside the marks [S15, F161, F162, F123, F192, F193]. That single gap covers BOTH of the disclosed floors the red team named: the property markdown sits inside it, because the property mark of Rp5,898bn is already deducted in arriving at the Rp36,934bn. The bull values the gap at book - the sourced floor the method card asks for rather than zero: Rp21.1tn is about Rp533 a share before the discount, about Rp373 at the bull's 30% discount and about Rp428 of target after the one-year roll [S15]. The base holds the same floor at zero and says so in section 4: the segment note does not disclose the composition of the Rp21.1tn, and part of it is the working capital that funds the businesses the marks already value, so marking it at book is a bull assumption about realisation, not a base-case asset. The Others/infrastructure run-rate is NOT a bull-only item: the base marks that block at the 30 September book, which already carries the nine-month Others profit of Rp2,558bn, up 36% [S14, F71]. The share-count shock carries the buyback acceleration; the Otoparts tender (maximum about Rp858bn [S13, F89]) sits outside the table because it is a transfer inside an already consolidated block. As in the bear, the engine does not reprice the listed stakes or the financing mark, so the floor leg and a re-rating of United Tractors or Astra Agro Lestari are carried in section 4 and 5, not in the tabulated bull.

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E set at +2%: the nine-month actual was Rp243,869bn [S15] and the third quarter alone Rp85,956bn, ahead of the second quarter's Rp79,245bn; management guides the fourth quarter to be supported by the same drivers that lifted the third - mining-contract volumes, the Martabe restart and continued automotive growth [S14]. A fourth quarter at the third quarter's run-rate gives full-year revenue of about Rp329.8tn, or +2% on FY2025. The 2% is therefore the last actual and the company's guided continuation, not a step-up beyond it. From FY2027E a 5% nominal growth, below the macro deck's 5.29% real GDP plus 3.28% inflation [KB macro deck] but above the old 4% - the auto franchise is recovering and the group now reports three core businesses [S2].

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: FY2026E set at 21.70%, the full-year rate implied by the nine-month actual (gross profit Rp52,008bn on net revenue Rp243,869bn, 21.3%) plus a fourth quarter at the third quarter's 22.75% (gross profit Rp19,556bn on revenue Rp85,956bn) [S15, S0]; the first half was depressed by the Martabe gold-mine outage and the RKAB coal quota, both of which eased in the third quarter [S14]. From FY2027E set at 21.63%, which is the FY2025 audited 22.09% (gross profit Rp71,444bn on net revenue Rp323,392bn [S6]) LESS the deck's rupiah path through the dollar-linked purchase book: related-party purchases were Rp84,937bn [S6, F21] and the house macro deck carries USD/IDR at 18,350 for FY2027E against an 18,012 spot, a 1.88% move, or Rp1,594bn on that flow, 0.46pp of FY2027E revenue. No pass-through into selling prices is assumed, because the 5% nominal revenue growth is the deck's inflation-plus-real path and contains no FX repricing [KB macro deck]; if the group reprices with the rupiah the 0.46pp comes back, and section 3 shows both. The level is therefore the last audited year's margin at the deck's currency - below, not above, both the FY2025 audited 22.09% and the third-quarter exit 22.75% - never a margin expansion against a weaker rupiah.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2026E set at 11.12% of full-year revenue, and the build is explicit: the nine months are the actual, selling and general expenses of Rp27,353bn on net revenue Rp243,869bn, or 11.22% of nine-month revenue [S15], and the fourth quarter is taken at the third quarter's 10.84% rate as promotional spend normalised, so the year blends to 11.12% of full-year revenue. From FY2027E the ratio glides from the third quarter's 10.84% actual to the FY2025 audited 10.14% [S6]: the nine-month 11.22% is depressed by the Martabe outage, which cut revenue (the same base effect the 21.3% nine-month gross margin shows), and the third quarter - after the gold restart and the coal-volume recovery - already ran at 10.84% [S15, S14]. Holding 11.22% to FY2035 would mean costs growing at revenue growth in perpetuity, a permanent step-up of about Rp3.2tn a year of EBIT against the audited ratio, which is an unsourced conservative drift, not the last actual. The glide is mechanical, not a forecast: costs grow with the macro deck's inflation (3.28%) against 5% nominal revenue [KB macro deck], a ratio factor of 0.984 a year, so the ratio falls from 10.84% to 10.66%, 10.49% and 10.32% over FY2028E-FY2030E and converges to the audited 10.14% in the long run. Real cost per unit of revenue is therefore held at the last actual, which is what the base-case card asks for.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 D&A of Rp17,871bn on net revenue Rp323,392bn from the audited expenses-by-nature note [S6] (the data pack carries no depreciation line for IDX filers); held flat, with capex at the same years level so the fixed-asset base is stable. H1-2026 D&A was Rp8.7tn on Rp157.9tn of revenue, in line [S5].

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: Held at the FY2025 audited actual from the expenses-by-nature note, capex Rp18,464bn on net revenue Rp323,392bn, or 5.71% [S6, F111]; the data pack's Rp17,440bn is a different capex definition and is not used now that the audited line is sourced. The group reported H1-2026 capital expenditure of Rp5.2tn on a cash basis, Rp6.4tn including leased assets and concession rights [S5], against Rp8.2tn in H1-2025 [S3], so the FY2025 ratio is at the top of the recent range and is not raised further.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: FY2026E rebuilt from the clean nine-month actual, not a rounded-up run-rate: share of joint-venture results was Rp8,127bn for nine months, up from Rp6,769bn a year earlier [S15], and other (expenses)/income net was a Rp2,429bn expense that includes the Rp2,963bn non-recurring impairment and fair-value charge [S15, S14]; adding that charge back leaves about Rp534bn of clean other income, so clean nine-month other non-operating income is Rp8,127bn + Rp534bn = Rp8,661bn [S15, S14]. Annualising the nine months at 4/3 gives Rp11,548bn, which is the FY2026E anchor (no unsourced fourth-quarter step-up). From FY2027E held at the FY2025 audited Rp10,702bn (profit before tax Rp49,288bn less EBIT Rp38,665bn plus finance costs Rp3,734bn less interest income Rp3,655bn [S6]), the joint-venture anchor, so the elevated 2026 JV print is not capitalised into the long run. The reset is not arbitrary: the nine-month 2026 joint-venture income of Rp8,127bn [S15] annualises at 4/3 to Rp10,836bn, 1.3% above the audited FY2025 anchor, so FY2027E at Rp10,702bn is the last actual JV run-rate rather than a haircut, and the 7% step down from FY2026E is the removal of the nine-month other-income annualisation, not a forecast of lower JV earnings. A JV-income shock is carried in the bear case.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: FY2026E set at 11%, the full-year rate implied by the actual nine months plus a fourth quarter at the third quarter's minority take: clean consolidated profit was about Rp27,036bn (reported Rp24,073bn plus the Rp2,963bn non-recurring charge) with about Rp2,471bn to non-controlling interests, a 9.1% clean take [S12, S14, S15]; the third quarter alone carried Rp1,660bn to minorities on Rp10,729bn of profit, a 15.5% take, as United Tractors' mining recovery lifted the 40.5% minority share [S0, S15]. A fourth quarter at that rate gives a full-year take of about 11%. The mining business collapsed in the first half while the wholly owned automotive and financing blocks grew, so the three-year-average 21.4% take is not the 2026 path. The reported nine-month take is 10.3% (Rp2,471bn on Rp24,073bn [S15, F170, F171]), so 11% is a deliberate fourth quarter at the third quarter's 15.5% take, 0.7pp above the reported actual and 1.9pp above the clean 9.1%. From FY2027E the take is held at that same 11% full-year rate, not the clean nine-month 9.1%, because the base carries the nine-month revenue, margin and cost ratios forward and does not add a mining recovery: a step to the FY2025 audited 18.49% (non-controlling interests of Rp7,436bn on consolidated profit for the year of Rp40,205bn [S6, F194, F195] - now sourced from the filing rather than the data pack) would require the segment-mix shift the base does not forecast. The mining-recovery sensitivity sits in the bull shock on revenue, margin and share count, where it belongs, rather than in the base through the minority ratio [S15, S6]. Value effect of the three choices, measured on the engine rather than asserted: the clean 9.1% take gives a target of Rp4,744, the 11.0% carried here gives Rp4,752, and the audited 18.49% gives Rp4,786, with the expected return 3.0% in all three [S0, S15]. The spread is a few tens of rupiah and the return does not move because the SOTP carries 96% of the weight and does not read the minority ratio at all - the choice shifts parent earnings and therefore the dividend split inside the one-year roll, nothing more. The input is not a valuation lever, and 11.0% is kept because it is the reported nine-month path plus a fourth quarter at the third quarter's observed take, not because it is the cautious end of the three.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: Set at the company-reported FY2025 payout ratio of 48% on the proposed Rp390 per share total dividend [S4, F90], not the 50% parent-entity cash payout (Rp16,426bn of parent cash dividends over FY2025 parent net profit [S6]) that was used before: the 48% is the policy ratio the company itself states, and the 50% is a parent-entity cash-flow ratio that mixes parent dividend income and one-off items. The same Rp98 interim was declared for FY2026 [S10], so the policy is being held, not raised.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: FY2026E set at -1.3%: nine-month EPS fell 11% to Rp541 while parent net profit fell 12%, implying a weighted-average share count about 1.3% lower year on year after the group completed Rp10.0tn of buybacks between November 2025 and September 2026 [S14]. FY2027E set at -4.0%: the Rp8tn Astra programme approved at the 17 July 2026 EGM [S8, S16] is carried to completion at the only sourced pace - the Group completed Rp10.0tn of buybacks over the eleven months to September 2026 [S14, F65], which is about Rp0.9tn a month. Rp8tn at that pace retires about 1.6bn shares, 4.0% of the 39.69bn count, in roughly nine months, inside FY2027E. The prior 2.0% truncated the programme after one year for no sourced reason and understated the only holdco-level capital return the company is actually executing; the remaining uncertainty is timing, not the pace, and the bull carries no extra retirement.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)

assumptions.label: Holding-company discount to SOTP
assumptions.basis: Set at 35% by a stated rule, not by the peer row (red team C9, accepted). The two observable bounds are the discount the market itself capitalises the parts at, 26% (the 6 November close of Rp5,000 against a NAV of Rp6,753 a share [S0, S15]), and the peer-set median excluding Astra's own row, 40%: the 14-name set shows a median of exactly 0.40, only TWO names at 0.30 (BRPT and CUAN), ADRO at 0.2311, BNBR at 0.38, BHIT at 0.40, IMJS at 0.60, ITMA at 0.741, PACK at 0.25 and ZBRA at 0.6625, and the median excluding ASII's own 0.35 is also 0.40 [cov_publish comps]. The base takes the MIDPOINT of those two bounds, 33.0%, and snaps it to the 5pp grid the peer set is quoted on, 35%; the 2pp snap is toward the peer median because the two name-specific facts widen the warranted discount (no dated narrowing catalyst, and related-party purchases of Rp84.9tn, about 30% of cost of revenue plus SGA [S6, F21]). That is the rule, and it is not circular: the peer set is used only for its EX-ASII median and the market-implied level enters as a bound, not as a target. The set is an anchor, not a validation - ASII's own 0.35 sits inside it, so reading the match as corroboration would be circular (red team C41, accepted) - and no ASII five-year observed discount series exists in the data pack, so VAL_HOLDCO_DISCOUNT rule 2's own-history test cannot be run and is disclosed rather than faked; the closest own series is the FY2025 P/B of 0.9x [S0]. We do not import the 40% median of small, illiquid names into a blue-chip whose NAV is mostly listed and marked at market, and we do not take the market's 26%, which is a price observation rather than a valuation. There is no dated discount-narrowing catalyst: the Rp8tn buyback approved at the 17 July 2026 EGM carries no end date or disclosed pace [S8, S14, S16]. Upstream cover is above one on the parent's accounts - FY2025 profit for the year of Rp19,886bn against Rp16,426bn of dividends paid [S6, F98, F22] - so the discount is not argued from dividend distress. The rule is price-sensitive by construction, and that is disclosed rather than denied: one bound is 1 minus price over NAV, so before the snap the target is about half the value the market's own discount implies and half the value the peer median implies, and it moves with the price. At the 6 November close the market bound is 26.0% (1 - 5,000 / 6,753) against the 40% ex-ASII peer median [S0, S15, cov_publish comps]. The peer leg is the one that does not depend on the price, and the snap takes the carried discount AWAY from the market level toward the peer median, so the target is not a reproduction of the close; but it is not independent of it either. The published bear carries the 40% peer median and the bull the 30% bottom of the cohort; the rating at 25/30/35/40/45% is shown in section 4. At the 40% fallback the target is Rp4,320 and the expected total return minus 5.6 per cent, still inside the HOLD band (section 4 shows it); REDUCE needs worse than minus 10%, first reached at 45%, where the grid gives Rp3,949 and minus 13.0 per cent. The prior draft's claims that the call turns REDUCE at the peer median, and that 40% gives minus eight per cent, were both wrong.

flags.justification: The VAL_HOLDCO_DISCOUNT card does not prescribe weights: rule 1 makes SOTP the engine for a listed parent of listed subsidiaries, with unlisted segments on their own cards, and the output contract is SOTP per share with per-component marks and methods; it does not call the multiples only cross-checks, and 96/2/2 is a house judgement, not a card rule. The judgement is that the peer-multiple and book legs are undiscounted while the parts carry a 35% discount, so a heavier weight on them would import the discount into the target; 2% each is kept so both are shown and footed in section 4. The change is conservative - it lowered the pre-roll value by about Rp850 against the old 60/25/15 blend - and section 4 argues it [S0, S15].
